papers.title: New Physics in Ultra-High-Energy Neutrino Flavor
papers.abstract: Neutrino flavor measurements test physics beyond the Standard Model that modifies neutrino production, propagation, or detection. IceCube has measured the flavor composition of the astrophysical neutrino flux up to PeV energies. Next-generation experiments will extend flavor measurements to the ultra-high-energy (UHE) regime, $100\,\mathrm{PeV}$-$10\,\mathrm{EeV}$, by combining in-ice radio detection with Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. We present the first study of the new-physics reach of these projected UHE flavor measurements. We take Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) as a benchmark, since its effects grow as a power of the neutrino energy. We find that UHE flavor ratios will be the most sensitive probe of LIV for operators of dimension four and higher, improving on current bounds from all sectors by up to twenty orders of magnitude. Three-flavor observables improve this sensitivity by up to an order of magnitude over Earth-skimming tau neutrinos alone.
papers.reason: This paper directly addresses neutrino flavor measurements and LIV probes in the UHE regime, which is very relevant to the reader's interest in BSM physics at neutrino experiments. [favorite author: Vedran Brdar]

summary.tldr: Combining projected ultra-high-energy in-ice radio and Earth-skimming tau-neutrino flavor measurements provides world-leading constraints on Lorentz invariance violation operators of dimension $d \ge 4$.
summary.novel_idea: This work presents the first study of physics beyond the Standard Model using projected ultra-high-energy (UHE) neutrino flavor composition measurements between $100\text{ PeV}$ and $10\text{ EeV}$. By combining in-ice radio detectors with Earth-skimming tau-neutrino experiments, the authors evaluate the full three-flavor triangle reach for Lorentz invariance violation (LIV). This leverages the strong $E^{d-3}$ energy scaling of higher-dimensional LIV operators to access previously unexplored parameter space.
summary.method: The authors parameterize isotropic LIV using an effective Hamiltonian with dimension $d=3\text{--}8$ operators. Cosmogenic neutrino fluxes and production redshift distributions are simulated using SimProp-v2r4 across three benchmark scenarios (optimistic, moderate, pessimistic). They then apply energy-averaged three-flavor transition probabilities to projected 68% and 95% CL sensitivity contours combining in-ice radio detectors (e.g., IceCube-Gen2, RNO-G) and Earth-skimming air-shower experiments (e.g., GRAND, POEMMA, TAMBO).
key_results: UHE flavor measurements improve existing bounds on LIV operators of dimension $d \ge 4$ by up to 20 orders of magnitude, reaching sensitivities down to $\sim 10^{-72}\text{ GeV}^{-4}$ for $d=8$.
Combining all three flavor channels enhances LIV sensitivity by up to an order of magnitude compared to using Earth-skimming tau-neutrino detectors alone.
Sensitivity to $e\tau$ and $e\mu$ LIV coefficients benefits most significantly from combining radio in-ice cascade/track channels with tau air showers.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to neutrino phenomenology and high-energy BSM probes, connecting to flavor composition analysis, cosmological neutrino propagation, and recent work by favorite author Vedran Brdar.
summary.caveats: Results depend on projected array configurations (such as GRAND antenna counts) and theoretical cosmogenic flux models, while assuming single-operator dominance and isotropic LIV couplings.

papers.title: Relativistic Second Random-Phase Approximation: Formalism and Applications to Giant Resonances
papers.abstract: We develop a self-consistent relativistic second random-phase approximation (RSRPA) based on covariant energy density functional with density dependent point-coupling interaction. The formalism extends the conventional simple configuration space composed of particle-hole ($p$-$h$) transitions by including two-particle-two-hole ($2p$-$2h$) configurations through a generalized Thouless ansatz and a time-dependent variational principle. To ensure consistency with the underlying mean-field ground state and avoid the double counting of correlations, we implement the subtraction method, in which the static contribution is removed from the residual interaction. The first applications of the RSRPA include studies of isoscalar and isovector giant monopole (ISGMR and IVGMR) and quadrupole resonances (ISGQR and IVGQR) in $^{16}$O, which demonstrate the importance of $2p$-$2h$ couplings to describe the fragmentation of the transition strength and the stabilizing role of the subtraction method.
papers.reason: This is highly relevant as it develops RSRPA for giant resonances, directly impacting the reader's core interest in neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling.

summary.tldr: A self-consistent Relativistic Second RPA framework incorporating $2p\text{--}2h$ configurations and a subtraction method successfully describes giant resonance fragmentation and spreading widths in $^{16}\mathrm{O}$.
summary.novel_idea: The paper introduces a fully self-consistent Relativistic Second Random-Phase Approximation (RSRPA) based on covariant energy density functionals with density-dependent point-coupling interactions. It systematically incorporates $2p\text{--}2h$ configurations alongside Dirac antiparticle-hole ($1\alpha\text{--}1h$) pairs via an extended Thouless theorem. Furthermore, it implements the subtraction method in a relativistic framework to remove static correlations, preventing double counting and matrix instabilities.
summary.method: The linearized equations of motion are derived using a time-dependent Dirac-Frenkel variational principle with the DD-PCX point-coupling functional. Calculations are performed for isoscalar and isovector monopole and quadrupole giant resonances (ISGMR, IVGMR, ISGQR, IVGQR) in $^{16}\mathrm{O}$ using spherical harmonic oscillator bases. Energy cutoffs for $2p\text{--}2h$ configurations up to $240\text{ MeV}$ are varied to evaluate numerical convergence.
key_results: Incorporating $2p\text{--}2h$ configurations generates substantial strength fragmentation and spreading widths, systematically lowering resonance centroid energies toward experimental data.
The subtracted extension (RSSRPA) eliminates unphysical complex eigenvalues and secures rapid convergence of strength distributions for $2p\text{--}2h$ cutoffs above $150\text{ MeV}$.
The diagonal approximation for the $2p\text{--}2h$ submatrix ($A_{22}$) works well for monopole modes but exhibits noticeable discrepancies in quadrupole channels.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly touches core research on nuclear electroweak responses, nuclear structure, and microscopic $2p\text{--}2h$ correlation modeling essential for neutrino-nucleus interaction calculations.
summary.caveats: The current implementation is restricted to spherical closed-shell nuclei and omits correlations in the Hartree reference ground state as well as $2\alpha\text{--}2h$ Dirac sea pairs.

papers.title: Tau polarization, new physics and CP violation in $\nu_\tau$-nucleus hyperon production
papers.abstract:
Charged-current interactions of the $	au$ neutrino are the least constrained sector of the Standard Model (SM) flavour structure, and the polarisation of the produced $	au$ lepton probes new-physics (NP) couplings, including CP-violating ones. Hyperon and charmed-baryon production gives access to the $u	o s$ and $d	o c$ transitions, but any measurement would be made on nuclei, which calls for a proper treatment of nuclear effects. We therefore study the sequential reactions $
u_	au\,{}^A Z	o	au^-(	o\pi^-
u_	au)\,\Lambda_c^+ X$ and $ ar
u_	au\,{}^A Z	o	au^+ (	o\pi^+ ar
u_	au)\,\Lambda X$ within the impulse approximation. The energy and angular distributions of the pion, which encode the $	au$ polarization, are derived for an arbitrary nuclear hole spectral function. As for free nucleons, an azimuthal pion asymmetry with respect to the plane spanned by the neutrino and the outgoing baryon is shown to remain. This is a CP-odd observable that vanishes in the SM, so that a nonzero value would signal CP violation irrespective of the hadronic form factors. Local Fermi gas results for ${}^{16}$O show that nuclear effects lower the reaction thresholds but leave the pion distributions, and hence the polarization information, close to their free-nucleon form. For representative NP scenarios the predicted asymmetries are at the percent level or below, with a magnitude that, in the $\Lambda$ channel, depends strongly on the transition form factors.
papers.reason: This is squarely in the reader's core interest, as it models tau-neutrino-nucleus interactions and CP violation in hyperon production. [favorite author: Jan Sobczyk]

summary.tldr: Nuclear impulse approximation calculations show that tau polarization observables in $\nu_\tau$-induced hyperon production on nuclei provide a zero-background, CP-odd probe of new physics.
summary.method: The authors integrate the sequential two-body production and decay phase space using an arbitrary nuclear hole spectral function evaluated in a Local Fermi Gas (LFG) model. The calculation incorporates the full dimension-6 NP effective Hamiltonian and lattice QCD / phenomenological $n\to\Lambda_c$ and $p\to\Lambda$ transition form factors. They extract averaged tau lepton polarization vector components (${\cal P}_L, {\cal P}_T, {\cal P}_{TT}$) and the resulting decay pion angular and energy distributions.
key_results: Nuclear binding and Fermi motion lower reaction energy thresholds from $8.3\text{ GeV}$ to $6.3\text{ GeV}$ for $\Lambda_c^+$ and from $4.0\text{ GeV}$ to $3.0\text{ GeV}$ for $\Lambda$ production.
Per-participant-nucleon pion differential distributions ($d\sigma/dE_\pi$ and $d\sigma/d\cos\theta_\pi$) retain shapes close to free-nucleon predictions.
The CP-odd pion azimuthal asymmetry $\Delta\sigma$ remains strictly zero in the SM, reaching percent or sub-percent levels in representative CP-violating NP scenarios.
summary.why_it_matters: A must-read paper authored by favorite authors J. Nieves and J. E. Sobczyk, directly addressing $\nu_\tau$-nucleus scattering, tau polarization, nuclear Fermi gas models, and CP-violating EFT probes relevant to DUNE, SHiP, and FPF.
summary.caveats: Transition form factors require analytic continuation to large spacelike $q^2$ introducing large uncertainties, and final-state rescattering (FSI) of the produced hyperon is omitted.

papers.title: Deeply inelastic scattering as an inverse problem
papers.abstract: A novel formalism for high-energy inclusive QCD processes based on analyticity of a scattering amplitude is proposed, which is conceptually distinct from the conventional factorization theorem. We illustrate how to analyze proton deeply inelastic scattering by means of the dispersion relations for double deeply virtual Compton scattering defined on a complex baryon mass plane. Inputting the perturbative results for the heavy baryon scattering amplitudes, we solve for the proton structure functions $F_2$ and $F_L$ in the nonperturbative low-mass region directly from the dispersion relations, i.e., as an inverse problem. The prior information, including the scaling of the structure functions in photon virtuality $Q^2$ and the quark counting rules for the threshold region with the Bjorken variable $x_B\to 1$, is incorporated. The only nonperturbative parameter at leading-power precision in $1/Q$ is the proton mass, with which we demonstrate the agreement between our predictions and the data for $F_2$ and $F_L$ at intermediate $x_B=0.18$-0.65 in a wide range of $Q^2=10^2$-$10^4$ GeV$^2$. Parton distribution functions can be extracted from the obtained structure functions as a byproduct of the analysis by treating the associated factorization formulas as another inverse problem. The same formalism with the pion mass as the nonperturbative parameter explains the data for the pion structure function $F_2^\pi$.
papers.reason: This is highly relevant as it proposes a new formalism for DIS, which is central to the reader's interest in neutrino-nucleus interactions and structure functions.

summary.tldr: Deeply inelastic scattering structure functions are calculated nonperturbatively from heavy-baryon Compton amplitude dispersion relations solved as an inverse matrix problem without requiring light-cone factorization or PDFs.
summary.novel_idea: The paper introduces a novel framework for high-energy inclusive QCD processes that replaces light-cone factorization with dispersion relations for double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS) evaluated on a complex baryon mass plane. By framing structure function extraction as an inverse problem with OPE inputs in the heavy-quark regime, nonperturbative structure functions are computed directly without introducing parton distribution functions (PDFs).
summary.method: Short-distance OPE inputs for heavy-baryon DIS are derived up to NLO in $\alpha_s$ at leading power in $1/Q$. Physical prior constraints are built into the formulation, including photon virtuality scaling, positivity, and threshold quark-counting laws $(1-x_B)^3$. The resulting ill-posed integral equation is solved numerically using the inverse matrix method expanded in generalized Laguerre polynomials.
key_results: Using only the proton mass $m_p$ as a nonperturbative parameter, the method accurately reproduces measured proton structure functions $F_2$ across $x_B = 0.18\text{--}0.65$ and $Q^2 = 10^2\text{--}10^4\text{ GeV}^2$.
Yields $F_L \approx 0.1$ at intermediate $x_B$, confirming the Callan-Gross relation $F_L \approx 0$ in the high-$Q^2$ Bjorken limit in agreement with HERA data.
Successfully describes the pion structure function $F_2^\pi$ at $x_\pi = 0.12$ using the pion mass $m_\pi$.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant to your interests in DIS cross sections, QCD short-distance factorization, hadron structure, and inverse problem methods for extracting nonperturbative hadronic functions.
summary.caveats: Applicable primarily at intermediate to large $x_B$ where valence quarks dominate; soft-parton contamination breaks the dispersion relation at small $x_B$, and $1/Q^2$ power corrections are currently neglected.

papers.title: Relating Short Range Correlated Pair Abundances to Electron-Scattering Cross Section Ratios
papers.abstract: We derive a coupled set of relations between inclusive and semi-exclusive nucleon-knockout electron-scattering cross-section ratios measured for any two nuclei in short-range-correlation (SRC) kinematics and the microscopic neutron-proton, (np-), proton-proton (pp-), and neutron-neutron (nn-) SRC pair populations in those nuclei. The derivation uses a factorized description of quasielastic scattering from SRC pairs and includes final-state interactions through nuclear transparency and single charge exchange. We show that the inclusive $(e,e')$, proton-knockout $(e,e'p)$, and neutron-knockout $(e,e'n)$ ratios are not independent: for any two nuclei where one is isospin symmetric ($N=Z$), two of these three observables determine the third within the model. For $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ and $^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}$, for example, the measured inclusive $(e,e')$ and proton-tagged $(e,e'p)$ ratios predict $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}/^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}(e,e'n)=1.35\pm0.07\,(\mathrm{exp})\pm0.15\,(\mathrm{model})$. A measurement of the $(e,e'n)$ ratio therefore provides a direct consistency test of the factorized pair-counting description. It also constrains the single-charge-exchange probabilities. Combining all three ratios with the two double-coincidence ratios determines the relative np-, pp-, and nn- SRC pair populations of any two nuclei. If one nucleus is isospin symmetric, any two of the three ratios suffice for the same result.
papers.reason: This is squarely in the reader's core interest: SRCs, electron scattering as a constraint, and nuclear structure for neutrino interactions.

summary.tldr: Factorized quasielastic electron scattering off short-range correlated pairs yields a coupled system of cross-section ratios where single-knockout channels are interdependent and constrain microscopic pair abundances.
summary.novel_idea: The authors derive a coupled system of algebraic equations connecting inclusive $(e,e')$, semi-exclusive single-nucleon knockout $(e,e'p), (e,e'n)$, and double-coincidence $(e,e'pp), (e,e'pn)$ cross-section ratios in short-range correlation (SRC) kinematics to microscopic $np$, $pp$, and $nn$ pair populations. They prove that for an isospin-symmetric reference nucleus, the three single-knockout/inclusive ratios are mathematically dependent, establishing a direct experimental closure test of SRC factorization.
summary.method: The derivation uses a factorized description of quasielastic scattering from 2N-SRC pairs in SRC kinematics ($x_B \ge 1.2$, $Q^2 \ge 1.5\text{ (GeV/c)}^2$, $p_{\text{miss}} \in [375, 700]\text{ MeV/c}$). Final-state interactions are incorporated through nuclear transparency and single charge exchange (SCX) probabilities. Algebraic elimination yields predictions for unmeasured channels and links single/double ratios to relative $np$, $pp$, and $nn$ abundances.
key_results: Establishes a consistency relation showing any two single ratios predict the third; measured $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}/^{40}\mathrm{Ca}$ inclusive $(e,e')$ and $(e,e'p)$ ratios predict $R_{48/40}(e,e'n) = 1.35 \pm 0.07\text{ (exp)} \pm 0.15\text{ (model)}$.
Demonstrates that measuring same-target proton-to-neutron ratios $R_{p/n}^A$ directly constrains SCX probabilities independently of SRC pair populations.

Proves that combining two target-to-target single ratios, two double-coincidence ratios, and one same-target ratio uniquely extracts the relative $np$, $pp$, and $nn$ pair populations between any two nuclei.
summary.why_it_matters: Touches core research topics in electron scattering constraints for neutrino interactions, nuclear $2p\text{--}2h$ modeling, short-range correlations, and the isospin composition of nuclear ground states.
summary.caveats: Assumes strict two-nucleon SRC dominance (neglecting 3N-SRCs and mean-field contamination), relies on transparency corrections, and truncates charge exchange at first order.

papers.title: Development and Experimental Characterization of a Compact $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O Photoneutron Source for Low-Energy Nuclear Recoil Calibration
papers.abstract: Calibrating the few-keV nuclear-recoil response of liquid xenon detectors calls for a low-energy neutron source. We have developed and characterized a $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O photoneutron source that converts the 2.615~MeV $\gamma$ rays from $^{208}$Tl into sub-MeV neutrons through the D($\gamma$,n)p reaction. After optimizing the D$_2$O geometry to balance neutron production against escape efficiency, we validated the chosen configuration experimentally. The forward emission rate is $1734 \pm 76~(\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 65~(\mathrm{sys.})~\mathrm{h}^{-1}$, and the spectrum unfolded from Bonner sphere data is concentrated at $0.17$--$0.22~\mathrm{MeV}$. In a 220~h exposure of PandaX-20T, the same configuration should provide about 1000 selected nuclear-recoil events. These results support the use of a long-lived $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O source for low-energy neutron calibration of large liquid xenon detectors.
papers.reason: This is directly relevant to the reader's core interest in low-energy neutrino physics on argon and calibration techniques for liquid argon detectors.

summary.tldr: This paper presents the development and characterization of a compact $^{228}\mathrm{Th}$--$\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}$ photoneutron source producing 0.17--0.22 MeV neutrons for low-energy nuclear recoil calibration in liquid xenon detectors.
summary.novel_idea: The authors develop a long-lived photoneutron source using $^{228}\mathrm{Th}$ (half-life 1.91 years) to produce sub-MeV neutrons via $^{2}\mathrm{H}(\gamma,\mathrm{n})\mathrm{p}$ driven by 2.615 MeV $\gamma$ rays from $^{208}\mathrm{Tl}$. This provides a significantly longer operational lifetime than standard $^{88}\mathrm{Y}$--$\mathrm{Be}$ sources (106.6 days) while avoiding broad high-energy neutron continua from $(\alpha,\mathrm{n})$ or fission sources.
summary.method: Geant4 simulations using the LEND physics list were employed to optimize the $\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}$ vessel geometry and source placement (1 cm from the forward face). The forward neutron yield was measured with a 4-cm polyethylene-moderated $^{3}\mathrm{He}$ proportional counter, and the neutron energy spectrum was unfolded from Bonner sphere spectrometer measurements using MAXED. Calibration performance in the PandaX-20T LXe TPC was evaluated using the BambooMC framework.
key_results: Measured forward neutron emission rate of $1734 \pm 76\text{ (stat.)} \pm 65\text{ (sys.)}\text{ h}^{-1}$ for a 72 kBq $^{228}\mathrm{Th}$ source.
Unfolded neutron energy spectrum is concentrated between 0.17 and 0.22 MeV, matching two-body photodisintegration kinematics.
Monte Carlo simulations for PandaX-20T show ~1000 single-scatter nuclear recoil events ($E_{\mathrm{NR}} > 1\text{ keV}_{\mathrm{nr}}$) in 220 hours under a ~30 Hz electron-recoil background.
summary.why_it_matters: While focused on LXe dark matter detectors (PandaX), the technique is relevant to low-energy nuclear recoil calibrations necessary for CEvNS and supernova neutrino detection in large noble liquid detectors.
summary.caveats: The low photodisintegration cross section of deuterium (~1.38 mb) requires intense $\gamma$-ray emission, generating a ~30 Hz electron-recoil background in the detector that demands dedicated tungsten shielding.

papers.title: Earth-sized tests of long-range neutrino interactions
papers.abstract: Neutrinos may experience a new long-range force that distinguishes their flavors, mediated by an ultralight neutral boson of a new $U(1)'$ gauge symmetry and sourced by the electrons and nucleons of ordinary matter. Atmospheric neutrinos that cross the Earth would then feel a flavor-dependent potential that alters their oscillations. When the range of the force is about one Earth radius or less, this potential varies from point to point along each neutrino's path, since it comes mostly from the matter near the neutrino. Earlier limits approximated it, either as constant along the path or as following the local density of matter. We compute it exactly at every point of each path, for the Earth model of the IceCube analysis and over the distribution of heights at which the neutrinos are produced, and use it to analyze the 8-yr public IceCube DeepCore sample with the systematic uncertainties of that analysis. For mediator masses from $10^{-15}$ to $10^{-9}$ eV, where the Earth alone sources the potential, we set upper limits at 90% confidence level on the coupling of eight of 14 $U(1)'$ symmetries, those whose potential differs between $\nu_\mu$ and $\nu_\tau$. A potential held at its value at the detector would weaken our limits by factors of about 1-3. Below about $10^{-11}$-$10^{-10}$ eV, depending on the symmetry, our limits are stronger than those from tests of the equivalence principle.
papers.reason: This paper uses IceCube data to test long-range neutrino interactions, which is squarely in the reader's interest in BSM physics at neutrino experiments.

summary.tldr: Using 8-year IceCube DeepCore data, this work sets limits on flavor-dependent long-range forces by evaluating the exact position-dependent Earth potential along neutrino paths rather than assuming a constant potential.
summary.novel_idea: This work presents the first atmospheric neutrino oscillation fit that tracks the exact position-dependent long-range potential along each trajectory inside a 12-layer PREM Earth model, integrating over the atmospheric production height distribution. Previous bounds assumed a constant potential fixed at the detector location or a simple local-density scaling. Exact trajectory integration is shown to strengthen limits on the gauge coupling $g'$ by factors of 1.2 to 3.0 for force ranges shorter than the Earth radius.
summary.method: The authors calculated closed-form radial integrals for the matter potential of $14$ $U(1)'$ gauge symmetries across mediator masses $m' \in [10^{-15}, 10^{-9}]$ eV. Flavor evolution was computed via Magnus expansion over MCEq atmospheric fluxes (SIBYLL-2.3d, GSF cosmic-ray model). A frequentist fit was performed on 200 bins of the 8-year public IceCube DeepCore dataset, profiling over oscillation and detector/flux systematic parameters.
key_results: Derived 90% C.L. upper bounds on $g'$ for 8 flavor-dependent symmetries that differentiate $\nu_\mu$ and $\nu_\tau$ potentials.
Limits on $g'\sqrt{|k|}$ for $L_\mu - L_\tau$ and $B - L_e - 2L_\mu$ are $\sim 1.45$ times stronger than for other flavor combinations due to maximal $\nu_\mu - \nu_\tau$ energy splitting.
Extracted limits outperform equivalence-principle tests (MICROSCOPE, Eöt-Wash) for mediator ranges exceeding 12 km ($m' < 10^{-11} - 10^{-10}$ eV).

No upper bounds are obtained for 6 symmetries that act on $
u_e$ alone ($k>0$ for $B-3L_e$, $L-3L_e$, etc.) because strong potentials decouple $
u_e$ without shifting the $
u_\mu$ survival minimum.
summary.why_it_matters: Crucial for neutrino BSM phenomenology, non-standard interactions (NSI), and atmospheric oscillation systematics. The methodology provides a baseline for exact path-dependent potential evaluation applicable to DUNE, Hyper-Kamiokande, and KM3NeT/ORCA.
summary.caveats: Limits rely on asymptotic Wilks-theorem thresholds ($\Delta\chi^2 = 1.64$), which display minor under-coverage (87% actual vs 90% nominal) in pseudo-experiments.

papers.title: A unified mean-field description of dense hadron matter constrained from $\chi$EFT and lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We construct a relativistic mean field theory (RMFT) of hadrons in an attempt to describe the confined phase of QCD across a wide range of temperatures and baryon densities. This includes the scalar and vector mesons interacting with baryons and resonances up to $3$ GeV, including those which are not yet discovered but predicted within the quark model and lattice QCD. The baryon--meson couplings are constrained through a two-stage Bayesian analysis. In the first stage, we constrain six different couplings in our theory using six nuclear empirical parameters inferred from the chiral effective field theory predictions of the energy per nucleon for pure neutron matter over baryon densities $n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]~\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$, employing a Gaussian-process likelihood to account for correlations in the input data. In the second stage, this posterior is set as the prior for constraining different baryon--meson couplings in our RMFT construction, using lattice QCD input. The resulting posterior provides substantially improved constraints for different baryon--meson couplings and non-linear meson self-interactions, which are consistent with the current astrophysical observations of neutron star masses, radii and tidal deformability parameters.
authors: Md. Emanuel Hoque (Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics/HBNI)
Arunava Mukherjee (Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics/HBNI)
Sayantan Sharma (The Institute of Mathematical Sciences/HBNI)
papers.reason: This is highly relevant as it uses chiral EFT and lattice QCD to constrain dense matter, which is central to the reader's interest in nuclear structure and neutrino-nucleus interactions.

summary.tldr: The authors construct a relativistic mean-field theory of dense hadronic matter up to 3 GeV resonances using a two-stage Bayesian framework constrained by chiral EFT and lattice QCD susceptibilities.
summary.novel_idea: The paper establishes a unified relativistic mean-field theory (RMFT) applicable from zero-temperature neutron stars to finite-temperature lattice QCD regimes. It uses a two-stage Bayesian analysis: Stage 1 constrains ground-state nucleon couplings via chiral EFT ($\chi$EFT) pure neutron matter EOS using a Gaussian-process correlation kernel; Stage 2 uses this posterior as a prior to constrain hyperon and resonance couplings using continuum lattice QCD conserved-charge susceptibility ratios at $T=135$ MeV.
summary.method: An extended Walecka-type Lagrangian was formulated including $\sigma, \omega, \rho, \sigma^*, \phi$ mesons coupled to all baryons and resonances up to 3 GeV. Stage 1 constrained 6 nuclear empirical parameters using $\chi$EFT energy per neutron data ($n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]\text{ fm}^{-3}$). Stage 2 constrained excited state scaling factors against lattice QCD cumulants $\chi_4^B/\chi_2^B$ and $\chi_{31}^{BS}/\chi_{11}^{BS}$ expanded to $\mathcal{O}(\hat{\mu}_B^6)$. The resulting EOS was applied to cold $\beta$-equilibrated neutron star matter matched to a sound-speed parametrization above $3-4\,n_{\mathrm{sat}}$.
key_results: Inferred 90% credible intervals for strange-baryon vector couplings: $g_{\omega Y} = 3.72\ [2.22, 5.63]$ and $g_{\rho Y} = 4.41\ [2.53, 7.00]$, showing strong hyperonic vector repulsion.
Scalar coupling to strange baryons $g_{\sigma Y}$ is constrained to a 90% upper limit of 2.82.
Predicted neutron star properties for $1.4\,M_\odot$ stars are $R_{1.4} = 11.52^{+1.11}_{-1.22}\text{ km}$ and $\Lambda_{1.4} = 245^{+260}_{-140}$, consistent with NICER and GW170817 measurements.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides rigorous constraints on nuclear interactions and equations of state derived jointly from ab initio $\chi$EFT and lattice QCD, relevant for nuclear structure, CEvNS modeling, and electroweak responses in dense media.
summary.caveats: Assumes universal coupling scale factors across all hyperon states in the 3 GeV resonance tower, and relies on Taylor-series extrapolations of lattice susceptibilities up to $\hat{\mu}_B = 3.0$ where truncation errors reach ~15%.

papers.title: Probing the internal structure of the $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon via its weak decays and lifetime
papers.abstract: The weak decay properties of the $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon play a crucial role in probing its internal structure and guiding experimental efforts. Using an effective Lagrangian approach, we systematically study its weak decays and lifetime by computing the widths for both three- and four-body final states, with amplitudes receiving contributions from single- and double-weak-vertex diagrams. We investigate the dependence of the decay properties on the binding energy ranging from a few MeV to over $100$ MeV. For weakly bound states ($E_b = 1$ and $20$ MeV), the three-body channels $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$, $\Omega \Xi \pi$, and $\Xi \Xi \bar{K}$ exhaust essentially the entire width, with the largest channel shifting from $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$ at $E_b=1$ MeV to $\Omega \Xi \pi$ at $E_b=20$ MeV. For deeply bound states ($E_b = 100$ and $120$ MeV), the $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$ channel is forbidden, and the dominant modes are $\Omega \Xi \pi$ and $\Xi \Xi \bar{K}$, while the double-weak-vertex channel $\Lambda \bar{K} \Lambda \bar{K}$ is found to be negligibly small. As the binding energy increases, the total lifetime extends from the order of $10^{-10}~\mathrm{s}$ to $10^{-9}~\mathrm{s}$. These distinct differences in decay patterns and lifetimes provide valuable theoretical reference values for experimental searches at RHIC and the LHC, and offer a clear discriminator between the compact hexaquark and weakly bound molecular interpretations.
papers.reason: Strongly relevant: weak decay properties of exotic nuclear states are directly related to the reader's work on nuclear de-excitation and neutrino-nucleus interactions.

summary.tldr: This study calculates multi-body weak decay widths and lifetimes of the $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon, establishing distinct decay patterns and lifetimes that discriminate between compact hexaquark and molecular structures.
summary.novel_idea: This work performs the first systematic calculation of 3-body and 4-body weak decay channels for the $J^P=0^+$ $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon ($S=-6$) across a broad range of binding energies ($E_b = 1 - 120$ MeV). It incorporates both single- and double-weak vertex mechanisms and accounts for empirical isospin-breaking effects in $\Omega \rightarrow \Xi \pi$ decays.
summary.method: An effective interaction Lagrangian for $\mathcal{D}_{\Omega\Omega}\Omega\Omega$ was constructed using a Gaussian cutoff form factor ($\Lambda = 0.8 - 1.2$ GeV). The effective coupling constant $g_{\mathcal{D}_{\Omega\Omega}\Omega\Omega}$ was determined via the Weinberg-Salam compositeness condition. Partial decay widths for tree-level and loop-induced rescattering diagrams were calculated by integrating matrix elements over 3-body and 4-body phase space.
key_results: For weakly bound states ($E_b = 1$ MeV), total width is dominated by $\Omega\Lambda\bar{K}$ (lifetime $\tau = 0.51-1.62 \times 10^{-10}$ s, decay length $c\tau = 1.53-4.86$ cm); $\Omega\Xi\pi$ dominates at $E_b=20$ MeV.
For deeply bound states ($E_b = 100-120$ MeV), $\Omega\Lambda\bar{K}$ is phase-space forbidden; dominant modes are $\Omega\Xi\pi$ and loop-induced $\Xi\Xi\bar{K}$.
Double-weak mode $\Lambda\bar{K}\Lambda\bar{K}$ and 4-body mode $\Xi\bar{K}\Xi\pi$ are negligibly small across all binding energies.
Lifetime extends by an order of magnitude from $\sim 10^{-10}$ s (shallow molecular state) to $\sim 10^{-9}$ s (deeply bound compact hexaquark).

papers.title: New measurement of BR$(K^+\rightarrow\pi^+\nu\bar\nu)$ at the NA62 experiment
papers.abstract:
The decay $K^+ightarrow\pi^+
u ar
u$ with a very precisely predicted branching ratio of less than $10^{-10}$ is one of the best candidates to reveal indirect effects of new physics at the highest mass scales. The NA62 experiment at the CERN SPS is designed to measure the branching ratio of the $K^+ightarrow\pi^+
u ar
u$ decay. A new measurement of its branching ratio based on the 20230-2024 dataset is presented. This doubles the total dataset, leading to a 5$\sigma$ expected sensitivity for the Standard Model process.
authors: Silvia Martellotti on behalf of NA62 Collaboration

summary.tldr: The NA62 experiment reports an updated measurement of $\mathrm{BR}(K^+\rightarrow\pi^+\nu\bar{\nu}) = 9.6^{+1.9}_{-1.8} \times 10^{-11}$ using 2016–2024 data, achieving a $5\sigma$ expected sensitivity for the Standard Model process.
summary.novel_idea: Presents the measurement of $\mathrm{BR}(K^+\rightarrow\pi^+\nu\bar{\nu})$ from the 2023–2024 NA62 dataset, which doubles the total statistics. Features hardware upgrades (hydrogen-filled KTAG detector, TDC/FELIX readout) and machine-learning kinematic reconstruction, improving $\pi^0$ rejection inefficiency to $(1.24 \pm 0.04) \times 10^{-8}$.
summary.method: Single-track events from a 75 GeV/c hadron beam decaying in a 65 m fiducial volume were selected. Missing mass $m^2_{\mathrm{miss}} = (p_K - p_{\pi^+})^2$ and $\pi^+$ momentum were categorized into two signal regions across 6 momentum bins. Normalization was anchored to $K^+\rightarrow\pi^+\pi^0$ events ($D=400$ trigger downscaling), and a profile likelihood fit across 21 data categories was performed.

Total 2016–2024 dataset yields 84 observed events with $30^{+4}_{-3}$ expected background and $43 \pm 1$ expected SM signal (>5$\sigma$ expected significance).
Measured branching ratio $\mathrm{BR}(K^+\rightarrow\pi^+\nu\bar{\nu}) = 9.6^{+1.9}_{-1.8} \times 10^{-11}$ (20% precision), consistent with SM predictions ($8 \times 10^{-11}$).

papers.title: Exploring the Pion Vector Form Factor Beyond the Physical Sheet
papers.abstract: Using analyticity and unitarity, we parametrise the pion vector form factor on the first and second Riemann sheets, below the inelastic $\pi\omega$ threshold. We fit this model-independent parametrisation to the available $\tau^-\to\pi^-\pi^0\nu_\tau$ data from ALEPH, Belle, CLEO and OPAL, together with spacelike data from NA7 and JLab, and extract the pole position and couplings of the $\rho^\pm$ along with the pion charge radius and low-energy $\pi\pi$ scattering parameters. Our results are independent of external scattering input and agree with the literature; in particular, we find $M_{\rho^\pm} = 762.07\pm 0.63$ MeV and $\Gamma_{\rho^\pm} = 143.62^{+0.79}_{-0.80}$ MeV. The parametrisation is publicly available in the EOS software.
papers.reason: The pion vector form factor is a critical input for neutrino-nucleus cross-section modeling and radiative corrections; this is highly relevant.

papers.title: Symmetry adapted tensor networks and quantum classical geometric learning for hadronic tomography: a proton construction
papers.abstract: We construct a calibrated model of the proton generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distribution (GTMD) $F_{1,1}$ in the real, staple-even valence-$u$ sector at zero skewness. Experimental measurements, lattice matrix elements, and phenomenological distributions enter through a single shared light-front state, organized as a symmetry-resolved tree tensor network in which color-singlet structure, exchange statistics, and the additive $J_z$ and $I_z$ charges are built in. Classical and quantum geometric nodes represent the residual transverse response. The GTMD is defined with soft subtraction, one-loop nonsinglet matching, NLO collinear evolution, and an explicit nonperturbative joint closure, so that each input is used with its own operator convention and scale. Calibrating against correlated ART25 transverse projections, HERA inclusive data, and lattice, elastic, and static information gives a simple picture. The forward inputs narrow the attainable transverse response by about $81\%$ at $x=0.4$. The simultaneous dependence on quark momentum and momentum transfer, however, is untouched by any of them: a deformation that leaves every present input invariant moves the nonforward value from $0.588$ to $0.378\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$. Dense momentum-space surfaces and finite-transfer-window phase-space maps show the structure this freedom controls. The tensor-network organization is chosen with composition in mind. The same shared subunits, operator hierarchy, and qualification protocol extend to the neutron, the spin-1 deuteron, and spin-$3/2$ nuclei, where the number of symmetry and exchange constraints grows quickly and a structural representation becomes the practical route. The quantum circuits are verified feature maps and state encodings; their capacity and cost are measured alongside the classical blocks.
papers.reason: The construction of GTMDs using tensor networks and lattice inputs is very relevant to the reader's interest in nucleon structure and neutrino-nucleus scattering.

papers.title: Entanglement, correlations, and resource costs for symmetry-adapted quantum simulations of light through medium-mass nuclei
papers.abstract: Entanglement governs both the classical cost of simulating correlated many-body systems and the quantum resources needed to treat them. In this work, we use nuclear symmetries to investigate the entanglement and correlations in nuclei using \textit{ab initio} symmetry-adapted no-core shell-model nuclear wavefunctions, illustrated here for $^{4,6,8}$He, $^8$Be, $^{12}\mathrm{C}$, $^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, and $^{48}$Ca. In this many-body approach, deformation and collectivity naturally emerge from the underlying chiral potential, and we show that the Sp(3,$\mathbb{R}$) basis concentrates the ground state in far fewer basis states than the SU(3) basis. We compute single-mode entropies and two-mode mutual information, and examine the organization of like-particle two-nucleon correlations into symmetry channels. Single-mode entropies are largest in the valence shells, while two-mode mutual information reveals substantial correlations both within and between shells. In all cases considered, the dominant pair correlations are captured by fewer SU(3) channels than angular-momentum channels, which reduces the number of variational parameters. Since the number of operator components within the channels is comparable in the two schemes for the heavier nuclei, this gives the SU(3)-coupling scheme a clear advantage. Fiedler ordering of the correlation graph with local refinement reduces the register ordering cost by a factor of 2 to 3 relative to the original shell ordering, and by 10 when two more shells are included in the register. Together, these measures link nuclear correlations to the selection of active modes and candidate excitation operators and to the design of quantum register layouts, offering guidance for the development of hybrid quantum-classical calculations of nuclei.

papers.title: Accelerating exact solutions of relativistic hydrodynamics and Levy-shaped freeze-out sources
papers.abstract: Femtoscopic measurements in heavy-ion collisions indicate that the pion source is L\'evy-stable rather than Gaussian, while the source radii still follow the hydrodynamic scaling $R^2\propto 1/m_T$. We call this coexistence the L\'evy hydro puzzle. For a perfect fluid with $\varepsilon=\kappa p$ and $p=nT$, flow and pressure form a closed system, and density and temperature can be ``dressed'' by an arbitrary comoving function, generalising a freedom known from Hubble-type solutions to arbitrary flows. We show that, at nonzero pair momentum, the source is bounded by the pressure on the freeze-out hypersurface, so its tail can never be heavier than the pressure tail. This yields a criterion for power-law source tails with two routes: either the outer flow is ultra-relativistic and the temperature grows at least linearly (Hubble-type solutions), or the flow is slow, the temperature uniform, and the proper acceleration falls off as $1/r$. We present a new family of relativistic, accelerating, self-similar potential flows ($\lambda$-PF) and a new dressing of Gubser's flow. The acceleration of $\lambda$-PF generates no power-law tail, but with a Hubble-type dressing its source tail is L\'evy-stable in a range of parameters, generalising the Hubble-type L\'evy source to accelerating cores. The isothermally dressed Gubser flow realises the $1/r$ route: its tail exponent lies outside the L\'evy-stable range, but over the measured range it gives L\'evy-like sources with $1/R^2$ linear in $m_T$. Thus L\'evy-like sources and the hydrodynamic $m_T$ scaling are compatible in perfect-fluid hydrodynamics, but hydrodynamics does not create the power-law tail: it is either inherited from a power-law pressure, requiring a $1/r$ acceleration, or put in through the dressing. We outline extensions towards non-spherical geometries and elliptic flow.
papers.reason: This is relevant to the reader's interest in relativistic modeling of scattering processes and nuclear freeze-out.

papers.title: Cross-shell excitations and the evolution of high spin states in $^{89}\mathrm{Y}$: A shell-model revisit
papers.abstract: Nuclei in the vicinity of $Z=38$--40 and $N=50$ provide an important testing ground for studying the evolution of nuclear structure across the proton subshell and neutron shell closure. In particular, $^{89}$Y offers an opportunity to investigate the inert core behaviour and effect of particle-hole excitations in generating the observed high spin states. In this work, we perform a systematic large-scale shell-model study of $^{89}$Y using different model spaces and well accepted effective interactions. Excitation energies, electromagnetic transition probabilities, and nucleon occupation probabilities are calculated and compared with available experimental data to explain the microscopic structure of the observed high spin states. The role of neutron excitations across the $N=50$ shell gap is examined in detail. A comparative analysis of the employed effective interactions is performed to assess their applicability in describing the spectroscopic properties of $^{89}$Y.
papers.reason: This is highly relevant as it performs a shell-model study of Y-89, which is central to the reader's interest in nuclear structure and neutrino-nucleus interactions.

papers.title: Self-Consistent Microscopic Description of the 146Sm Half-Life for Early Solar System Chronology
papers.abstract: The extinct \textit{p}-process radionuclide $^{146}$Sm, decaying to $^{142}$Nd, is a key short-lived chronometer for the formation and early evolution of terrestrial planets and planetesimals. However, there has been a long-standing discrepancy in both the experimental measurements and the theoretical evaluations of the $^{146}$Sm half-life. To address this, a self-consistent microscopic framework for $\alpha$ decay is developed in this work, in which the $\alpha$ particle is treated as a four-nucleon quartet. Its formation amplitude in the nuclear interior is constructed from a coherent superposition of multiple pure single-particle configurations weighted by the pairing occupation amplitudes. Coupling this shell amplitude to the $\alpha$ cluster that survives in the low-density surface region yields a self-consistently determined two-state (shell~$\oplus$~cluster) preformation weight and effective potential. The calculated half-lives for the neighboring emitters of $^{146}$Sm are in good agreement with the measured values. Cross-validation over the neighboring emitters reproduces each excluded half-life without any nucleus-specific adjustment, and yields $^{146}$Sm predictions consistent to within $\pm 6\%$ of the resulting half-life $T_{1/2}=75.1^{+6.1}_{-5.6}$~Ma. This provides a solid calibration for theoretical studies of the early solar system.
papers.reason: Precision nuclear physics and decay constants are highly relevant for the reader's interest in nuclear structure and low-energy neutrino physics.

papers.title: Low-lying doubly charmed strange baryons via QCD sum rules
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the masses of the low-lying doubly heavy baryons and their $B^*(3/2^+)\to B(1/2^+)\gamma$ radiative transitions within QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules (LCSR). By constructing mixed interpolating currents, we obtain $M_{\Xi_{cc}}=3.62^{+0.14}_{-0.15}$ GeV, $M_{\Xi_{cc}^*}=3.72^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ GeV, $M_{\Omega_{cc}}=3.72^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, and $M_{\Omega_{cc}^*}=3.82^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, together with their doubly bottom partners around $10.27$--$10.34$ GeV. The extracted masses are compatible with the observed $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ states and predict hyperfine splittings of about $101^{+27}_{-11}$ MeV and $99^{+11}_{-12}$ MeV for the $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ systems, respectively. Using these inputs, we derive the LCSR for the electromagnetic form factors and obtain radiative widths $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*++}\to\Xi_{cc}^{++}\gamma)=5.25^{+8.57}_{-3.62}$ keV, $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*+}\to\Xi_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.31^{+0.84}_{-0.25}$ keV, and $\Gamma(\Omega_{cc}^{*+}\to\Omega_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.41^{+0.67}_{-0.30}$ keV, while the corresponding doubly bottom widths are at the $0.002$--$0.01$ keV level. We find that the magnetic-dipole contribution dominates, whereas the electric-quadrupole form factor is numerically small. The light- and heavy-quark photon-emission terms can interfere or enhance significantly, and the heavy-quark contribution cannot be neglected in radiative transitions. These results provide useful theoretical guidance for future searches for spin-$3/2$ doubly heavy baryons through radiative decay modes at LHCb, Belle II, and other experimental facilities.
papers.reason: QCD sum rules for heavy baryons are highly relevant to the reader's interest in nucleon/baryon structure and resonance production.

papers.title: Revisiting the Isospin Quartic Term of the Nucleonic Matter Equation of State in the Walecka Model
papers.abstract: The fourth-order nuclear symmetry energy $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ is generally regarded as a small correction to the quadratic symmetry energy, but its magnitude, density dependence, and implications for neutron stars (NSs) remain unconstrained. Within the nonlinear Walecka model, we derive an analytical expression for $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ and construct 3000 equations of state (EOSs) constrained by nuclear data and astrophysical observations. We find that: (1) At saturation density, $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ can reach $6$\,MeV or higher, well above the commonly expected $2$\,MeV, while relatively large values can remain compatible with microscopic calculations. (2) Over NS densities, $|E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)|$ generally stays below $20$\,MeV but can reach about $25\%$ of the symmetry energy. (3) EOSs with $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)\gtrsim2\,\rm{MeV}$ can exhibit positive symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ while satisfying the GW170817 tidal deformability constraint, potentially relaxing the previously inferred preference for negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$. (4) The density derivatives of $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$, particularly its curvature $K_{\rm{sym,4}}$, can contribute substantially to the fourth-order isospin incompressibility. (5) Variations in $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ across selected EOSs can change the low-density squared speed of sound by $40\%$ or more. Higher-order symmetry energies also affect the proton fraction and NS core-crust transition. Thus, even a modest fourth-order contribution to the EOS can significantly influence the response and composition of asymmetric nucleonic matter, highlighting the importance of going beyond the quadratic approximation.
papers.reason: Nuclear equation of state and symmetry energy are critical for supernova neutrino physics and argon-based experiments.

papers.title: Dark matter evolution in stellar objects: A Boltzmann transport approach
papers.abstract: Dark matter (DM) captured by stars offers a way to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study the evolution of captured DM with the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), which follows both the abundance and the phase-space distribution of the bound particles from capture toward a stationary state. Averaging over orbital motion, we write the BTE as a master equation in energy and angular momentum that includes capture, scattering between bound orbits, annihilation and evaporation. Applying it to the Sun, we find that captured DM does not thermalize within the solar age when its scattering on nuclei is rare. The bound DM then remains much more extended than the isothermal distribution assumed in the classical treatment, and its annihilation rate can be suppressed by many orders of magnitude. We also apply the BTE to the inelastic Higgsino interpretation of the recent LUX-ZEPLIN result, which involves two DM components coupled through inelastic scattering. The thermal motion of solar nuclei opens capture channels that are closed for nuclei at rest and strengthens the constraint on the mass splitting by tens of keV.
papers.reason: Dark matter capture in stars is a key area for neutrino-related dark matter searches.

papers.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
papers.abstract: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $\pi\pi N$ effects on top of the two-body $\pi N$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $\pi\Delta(1232)3/2^+$, and $\pi N(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $\pi N$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $\pi\Delta$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.
papers.reason: The Roper resonance is a key feature in neutrino-nucleus resonance production models; this paper's treatment of three-body dynamics is highly relevant.

papers.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
papers.abstract: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW. Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2\sigma$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.
papers.reason: This paper directly addresses low-energy neutrino detection and global fits to data, which is highly relevant to the reader's interest in low-energy neutrino physics and phenomenology.

papers.title: Dual-species atom interferometry for axion dark matter
papers.abstract: Atom interferometers are sensitive to oscillations of the masses and transition frequencies of atoms, which can be induced by axion dark matter. The main limitation is the sensitivity to gravity gradient noise (GGN). We propose a dual-species atom interferometry sequence that provides a suppression of GGN by up to three orders of magnitude and a sensitivity enhancement via the mass difference of the two atoms. We show that, under realistic experimental assumptions, a 10m-baseline dual-species atom interferometer is more sensitive to the axion gluon coupling than a 100m single-species gradiometer. Including a comprehensive noise analysis, we demonstrate that the Very Long Baseline Atom Interferometer (VLBAI) in Hannover with a baseline of 10m can probe the axion decay constant at levels almost competitive with leading laboratory constraints. The proposed 100m-baseline Atom Interferometer CERN Experiment (AICE) can extend this sensitivity by up to two orders of magnitude, surpassing laboratory constraints for axion masses of $10^{-19}\;\text{eV}/c^2 \lesssim m_a \lesssim 3\times10^{-15}\;\text{eV}/c^2$.
papers.reason: Precision atomic probes of new physics are a high-interest area for this reader. [favorite author: Elina Fuchs]

papers.title: Chains of Vector-like Leptons at Colliders
papers.abstract: Vector-like leptons (VLLs) are predicted in the chain flavor models, which possess characteristic features to explain the mass hierarchy and mixing of the fermions in the Standard Model (SM). We investigate the production and decay of the VLL chains and quantify the discovery potential at the LHC, FCC-hh, and lepton colliders. The resonant mass sets the new physics scale responsible for the fermion mass generation. The observation of the VLL multiplets associated with each lepton flavor yields the chain structure. The mass difference among the VLL multiplets determines the hopping parameter that gives the power-law pattern for the observed SM fermion masses. The single VLL production via vector boson-lepton fusion directly measures the partial width, equivalently the new Yukawa coupling and the VLL mass hopping parameter. At hadron colliders, the leading production mechanism is pair production via their gauge interaction. We find that HL-LHC may have the sensitivity to reach the chain scale of $800-900\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and FCC-hh reaches $>2.5\,\mathrm{TeV}$. In $e^+e^-$ and $\mu^+\mu^-$ colliders, VLL pair production is a clear discovery channel once the threshold is reached. Single production via $Z$-lepton fusion becomes more accessible owing to a lower mass threshold and extends signal discovery to the collider kinematic limit.

papers.title: $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$, Radiative Dirac Neutrinos, and Flavor Physics from Leptoquarks
papers.abstract:
Leptoquarks provide a common framework for addressing flavor anomalies, rare meson decays, and neutrino-mass generation. We study a model with two mixed scalar leptoquarks and three right-handed neutrinos that generates radiative Dirac neutrino masses and contributes to $B^+	o K^+
u ar
u$, charged-lepton flavor violation, and the effective number of relativistic species. We show that the model can accommodate the Belle~II measurement of $B^+	o K^+
u ar
u$ while satisfying the $\mu	o e\gamma$ bound and the cosmological constraint on $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}}$. When both leptoquark masses exceed approximately $12$--$14\,\mathrm{TeV}$, the new contribution to the $B$-meson decay becomes too small, and the prediction approaches the SM value, which lies below the Belle~II measurement. Interestingly, the lower bounds on the leptoquark mass scale derived from $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ can be stronger than those from direct collider searches.

papers.title: Slow Macroscopic Rotations of Neutron Stars With a Deformed Effective Surface
papers.abstract: The macroscopic model for a neutron star (NS) as a finite perfect fluid at the equilibrium is extended to rotating deformed systems by incorporating the linear perturbation expansion over a small frequency $\omega$ near the Schwarzschild gravitational metric within the effective-surface (ES) approach. The NS angular momentum $I$ and moment of inertia (MI) for a slow stationary azimuthal rotation around the symmetry axis is calculated by using the Kerr metric approach in spheroidal coordinates, and compared with the spherical results. The gradient surface terms of the macroscopic NS energy density $\mathcal{E}(\rho)$ (Equation of State) are taken into account along with the volume ones at the leading order of the leptodermic parameter $a/R \ll 1$, where $a$ is the ES crust thickness and $R$ is the NS effective radius. The analytical macroscopic NS MI expressions, $\Theta = dI/d\omega = \widetilde{\Theta}/(1-\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi})$, have been obtained in terms of the statistically averaged MI, $\tilde{\Theta}$, and its time and azimuthal-angle $t,\varphi$ correlation, $\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi}$, as sums of the volume and surface components. The MI $\Theta$ is changed significantly as function of the effective radius $R$ and deformation parameter because of a strong gravity. We found the additional narrower constraints for the NS radius due mainly to the $t,\varphi$ correlations and surface contributions and NS surface deformation. The adiabaticity conditions for application of the linear perturbation theory is carried out for several neutron stars with a strong gravity and relatively large rotation periods.
papers.reason: This is relevant to the reader's interest in dense matter and nuclear structure, as it models neutron star properties.

papers.title: A triple-threat challenge for $\mathit{T}$ and $\mathit{S}$ at two loops
papers.abstract: In the $Z_2$-symmetric real singlet-scalar extension of the Standard Model (SM), the oblique parameters $\mathit{T}$ and $\mathit{S}$ first receive contributions at two loops, making their precise prediction a challenge. We take on this challenge with a triple threat. First, we perform an exact two-loop calculation in the full theory. Second, we derive the logarithmically enhanced terms from a general argument, according to which the singlet rescales the Higgs couplings to the electroweak gauge bosons and thereby spoils the cancellation of ultraviolet divergences between Higgs and Goldstone contributions. Third, we reproduce the results in the SM effective field theory, where the logarithms and mass-dependent terms stem from one-loop matrix elements of the dimension-six operator that modifies the Higgs kinetic term, and the remaining constants from two-loop matching. Our calculations provide a blueprint for new-physics scenarios in which the leading effects modify the Higgs couplings in a custodially symmetric way, so that custodial-symmetry violation, and hence $\mathit{T}$, arises only beyond one loop. Finally, we derive constraints from current and projected electroweak precision measurements and show that effects beyond dimension six matter for light singlets.
papers.reason: This is relevant to the reader's interest in EFTs and precision electroweak physics.

papers.title: Discovering new physics with semitauonic $b$-hadron decays
papers.abstract: Anomalous lepton flavor universality violation (LFUV) observed in semileptonic decays of beauty hadrons may be the first signal of new physics (NP) beyond the Standard Model. We review the essential theoretical concepts and experimental considerations required for self-consistent and unbiased NP interpretations of these LFUV anomalies. We examine the status of present-day analyses, and assess the core challenges to the future precision studies that will be required to conclusively establish or reject an NP signal, as well as promising strategies to resolve them.
papers.reason: High relevance to flavor physics and potential BSM signals, which the reader tracks for novel phenomenological angles.

papers.title: The Curious Case of Anapole Dark Matter at LZ: Minimal, Elastic and Testable
papers.abstract: Majorana fermions can carry neither charge nor dipole moments, leaving the anapole moment as their leading electromagnetic interaction. A stable Majorana fermion is therefore a minimal realization of electromagnetically interacting dark matter. The momentum dependence of the anapole interaction produces a harder recoil spectrum than standard momentum-independent interactions. We show that this makes elastically scattering anapole dark matter a viable interpretation of the single high-energy nuclear-recoil event recorded by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, in a region where almost no background is expected. Curiously, the same coupling that fits the LZ data also yields the observed dark matter abundance at a mass of about 300 GeV, and is consistent with collider searches and indirect detection. The scenario is testable, predicting further events at lower energies, which the full LZ run will probe and a next-generation detector such as XLZD will decisively test.
papers.reason: Direct detection phenomenology is highly relevant, especially given the connection to LZ and potential neutrino-like scattering signatures.

papers.title: High Energy Asymptotics of Quark-Gluon Correlations
papers.abstract: The internal structure of the proton is encoded not only in single parton densities, but also in the quantum interference between distinct partonic configurations. We study the high energy behavior of this interference by focusing on flavor-nonsinglet quark-gluon correlations relevant to transverse spin phenomena. By establishing recursive factorization at double logarithmic accuracy in the presence of a coherent gluon insertion, we derive infrared evolution equations for the Qiu-Sterman function and its chiral odd Boer-Mulders counterpart. We find that these twist-3 functions share the leading small $x$ intercepts of their respective twist-2 counterparts, but acquire an additional $1/\ln(1/x)$ suppression due to the color structure of the coherent gluon insertion. These results may guide small $x$ extrapolations of quark-gluon correlations at the Electron Ion Collider.
papers.reason: Twist-3 functions and small-x evolution are directly relevant to the reader's interest in nucleon structure and neutrino-nucleus scattering.

papers.title: Inelastic Scalar Dark Matter in a Gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ Model and its LZ Phenomenology
papers.abstract: We study inelastic scalar dark matter (DM) in a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ model motivated by the high-energy recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ). The model introduces two complex scalars, $\Phi$ and $S$, charged under $U(1)_{B-L}$. The scalar $S$ is responsible for spontaneous symmetry breaking, while the two real components of $\Phi$, $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$, serve as DM. This two-component DM framework accommodates both exothermic and endothermic scenarios. In the exothermic scenario, the lifetime of the heavier state $\phi_1$ exceeds the age of the Universe, and both states contribute to the present-day DM abundance. In the endothermic scenario, the abundance comes almost entirely from the lighter state $\phi_2$. We investigate the thermal history of the dark sector and find that the two scalars have approximately equal abundances at freeze-out. We identify parameter regions that reproduce the observed relic abundance. We calculate the nuclear recoil spectra, perform a three-bin likelihood analysis, and obtain the best-fit points interpreting the LZ signal in both scenarios.

papers.title: Search for gravitational wave coincident neutrinos in DEAP-3600
papers.abstract: We searched DEAP-3600 data for neutrino signals coincident with gravitational waves from compact object mergers observed by the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA collaborations (LVK). While mergers involving neutron stars are expected to produce neutrinos, these have never been detected. The DEAP-3600 experiment is sensitive to electron neutrinos as recently observed through charged current neutrino absorption on its $^{40}$Ar target. Between 2016 and 2020, the detector recorded data during seven compact merger events involving neutron stars that were observed gravitationally by LVK. Upon examination, there is no statistically significant evidence of neutrinos from any of the mergers analyzed. Exclusion limits are set on the electron neutrino fluence, e.g. from GW170817 in the mono-energetic model at $6.8\times10^{12}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$ ($1.8\times10^{10}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$) for 10 MeV (100 MeV) neutrinos.

papers.title: Solar Neutrinos at the ESS{\nu}SB experiment
papers.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of the ESSnuSB large underground water-Cherenkov (WC) detector to two key solar neutrino signatures: the MSW spectral upturn in the $^8$B electron neutrino survival probability $P_{ee}(E_\nu)$, and the first direct observation of the rare hep neutrino flux. The analysis incorporates detector systematic uncertainties (energy resolution and flux normalization) and models environmental backgrounds from cosmic-ray muon spallation and $^{222}$Rn contamination. We adopt a shape-driven analysis strategy with a floating overall normalization, so that the discovery power relies on the spectral distortion rather than on the absolute event rate. In a realistic scenario with 90% spallation rejection efficiency, informed by the Super-Kamiokande experience and recent JUNO analyses, residual spallation backgrounds prevent either signal from reaching $5\sigma$ significance within 20 years of exposure. For the hep flux, we present a detailed sensitivity study to both its discovery and its precision, and quantify how the required spallation veto efficiency and recoil energy threshold jointly determine the achievable significance for both signals. At the adopted thresholds, discovery-level sensitivity for both signals requires approximately 99% spallation rejection over a 20-year exposure.

papers.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
papers.abstract: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $\nu_\tau$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.

papers.title: Learning to Calibrate Jet Energies
papers.abstract: Hadronic jets are produced copiously at the Large Hadron Collider, and are a vital element of its physics program. Accurate reconstruction of their energies is therefore crucial, including correction for pile-up, detector response and data-simulation differences. Currently, each correction is performed by fitting parametric functional forms, an approach which is effective but can be fragile and challenging to extend. We present a prototype machine-learning pipeline which performs pile-up dependency removal, absolute corrections and data-mc corrections. No functional form is imposed on the correction, additional features can be easily added, and the pipeline matches or exceeds the performance of the functional approach at nearly every stage.

papers.title: Lepton flavor violation at mass dimension eight
papers.abstract: Operators that violate lepton flavor first arise at mass dimension $d=5$ in the Standard Model Effective Field Theory, while charged lepton flavor violation first appears at $d=6$, inducing the typical exotic particle decays currently probed by experiments. Operators at $d=8$ carry the same quantum numbers as those at $d=6$ and are thus seemingly doomed to be subleading corrections. After (re)deriving the complete set of tree-level UV completions for lepton-flavor-violating $d\leq 8$ operators via heavy scalars and fermions, we show that some UV completions exclusively generate $d=8$ flavor violation at tree level, with $d=6$ contributions suppressed by loop factors and, in some cases, unrelated couplings. Such accidentally protected $d=8$ scenarios enlarge the set of testable lepton-flavor-violating operators.

papers.title: Novel method for measuring the isovector partner of X(3872)
papers.abstract: The predicted isovector partner of the $X(3872)$, denoted as $W_{c1}$, is expected to produce only a relatively weak structure near the charged $D \bar{D}^*$ threshold, making its experimental identification challenging. In this work, we explore the triangle singularity (TS) mechanism as a means of enhancing the sensitivity to the $W_{c1}$ in the decays $B^0 \to \pi K \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$. We investigate the $D_{s1}(2536) \bar{D}^*$ triangle rescattering mechanism, incorporating the coupled-channel $D \bar{D}^*$ scattering amplitudes obtained from the Lippmann-Schwinger equation. The interplay between the TS and the coupled-channel dynamics produces characteristic structures in the $K \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$ invariant mass distributions associated with the $X(3872)$ and its isovector partner $W_{c1}$. In particular, the charged-channel contribution exhibits a distinct structure sensitive to the nearby $W_{c1}$ pole. Our results demonstrate that the TS mechanism provides a promising way to probe the otherwise weak manifestation of the $W_{c1}$, offering a complementary experimental strategy for searching for this predicted state at Belle II and LHCb.

papers.title: On the reduction of negative-weight events in MC@NLO with Machine Learning techniques
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that Machine Learning techniques can be successfully employed to re-define ${\mathbb S}$-event MC@NLO short-distance cross sections in a manner which in most cases leads to a reduction of their fractions of negative weights, with a modest increase of computational costs. We work with both Decision Trees and Normalizing Flows, and consider several processes, in both $e^+e^-$ and $pp$ collisions, that vastly differ in their kinematical and dynamical complexity. In those situations where the ML-induced reduction of negative weights is not significant we are able to identify the primary reason(s) for this behaviour, thus paving the way for it to be addressed in future studies. This work is still to be considered as a proof of concept, given that the proposed methodology is not implemented in a public code; yet, it is based upon a fully realistic simulation environment, in which no simplifying assumptions are made.

papers.title: A Non-Relativistic Model of Heavy Quarkonium
papers.abstract: We develop a non-relativistic, spin-dependent, phenomenological model of heavy quarkonium. The model is based on a hydrogen-like Schr\"odinger equation derived from a spin-dependent Hamiltonian that includes a hyperfine spin--spin interaction term. The resulting system is solved using matrix mechanics by diagonalizing the Hamiltonian to obtain the energy spectrum. The energies are further optimized using variational methods. Spin--orbit corrections are included at first order in perturbation theory. The resulting spectrum shows good agreement with experimental data for conventional heavy quarkonium states. The framework combines matrix mechanics, variational methods, and perturbation theory, and is therefore suitable for students familiar with quantum mechanics.

papers.title: A Scattering Phase Space Primer
papers.abstract: The kinematic phase space is fundamental to all particle scattering processes across experiments - from lepton and hadron colliders to dark matter searches. While $2 \to 2$ scatterings are well understood, the simplest non-trivial case of three-body final states presents major analytic challenges that are typically circumvented by numerical methods. This paper provides the first comprehensive analytic treatment of $2 \to 3$ phase space and cross section distributions that uses a non-constant matrix element and keeps all particle masses non-zero. This is fundamental for an accurate description of crucial configurations for Beyond Standard Model searches, e.g. Vector Boson Fusion. Using Gram Determinants as our primary language for Lorentz-invariant kinematics, we derive exact, closed-form expressions for differential cross section distributions and explicitly construct the complete physical phase space boundaries. This paper serves as both a pedagogical introduction and a practical reference for the analytic computation of realistic $2 \to 3$ processes, showing how the $m\neq0, |{\cal M}|\neq 1$ problem is computationally tractable through proper kinematic methods. The results apply universally across all $2 \to 3$ scatterings regardless of center-of-mass energy, particle masses, or interaction type.

papers.title: Probing gluon saturation with forward heavy-flavor correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy-flavor azimuthal correlations as probes of gluon saturation in high-energy $p$+$p$ and $p$+Pb collisions within the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. Heavy flavor has several advantages: heavy-quark production is especially sensitive to the small-$x$ gluon distribution of the target, while the quark mass suppresses collinear radiation. Further, the heavy meson carries a large fraction of the momentum of its parent quark, so that the meson pair follows the partonic kinematics more closely than for light hadrons. We present the first calculation of heavy-meson pair correlations over the full azimuthal range that combines small-$x$ evolution from an initial condition constrained by HERA data with Sudakov resummation near the back-to-back limit. It provides a good description of the $D$-$\bar D$ and $b$-hadron pair correlations measured by LHCb. In contrast to the light-flavor case, we predict, in addition to a suppression of the away-side yield in $p$+Pb relative to $p$+$p$ collisions by about $15\%$, a broadening of the peak by approximately $10\%$ to $25\%$ for Gaussian fits near $\Delta\Phi=\pi$, which makes heavy-flavor correlations a promising observable in the search for gluon saturation.

papers.title: Connecting Electroweak Fine-Tuning, Tens-of-GeV Dark Matter, and Exotic Higgs Decays in the GNMSSM
papers.abstract: In the general next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model (GNMSSM), we connect electroweak fine-tuning, a singlino dark matter candidate with mass around tens of GeV, and Exotic Higgs Decays, identifying a natural region characterized by the mass hierarchy $m_{\tilde{S}}<m_{\tilde{B}}<m_{\tilde{H}}$ and $\mu_{\rm tot}\in [200, 500]$ GeV. For fine-tuning measure $\Delta \leq 40$, the branching ratio $\mathrm{Br}(h\to a_sa_s)$ falls in the range 7\%$-$25\%, with the pseudoscalar mass $m_{a_s}$ lying mostly between 10 and 20 GeV. This region splits into two viable scenarios consistent with LZ 2024 direct detection: one where the lightest CP-even Higgs $h_1$ is SM-like ($h_1$ case), and another where the second-lightest $h_2$ is SM-like ($h_2$ case). LHC searches for $h\to a_sa_s \to b\bar{b}\tau^+\tau^-$ exclude 12\% (10\%) of samples with 12 GeV $\leq m_{a_s} \leq$ 15.5 GeV in the $h_1$ ($h_2$) case, while a substantial fraction remains accessible at the HL-LHC in the $h_2$ case. Our analysis unifies naturalness, dark matter, and observable exotic Higgs decays, yielding concrete targets for future experiments.
